title: try4-expert-bootstrap-round2
goal: Learn a formal expert experience workspace from the workbook, the two finished expert Word documents, and the two blank templates, so that a blank agent can later generate the required Word outputs in one uninterrupted session.

capabilities.title: DOCX capability package
capabilities.description: Use the registered DOCX skill package to inspect templates, inspect finished Word references, and generate or edit final Word outputs through formal capability assets instead of hidden runtime memory.

capabilities.title: XLSX capability package
capabilities.description: Use the registered XLSX skill package to inspect workbook structure and source values through formal capability assets.

validators.title: Learned expert workspace layout is valid

initialGraph.planner_summary: Start by extracting stable obligations from the workbook, expert references, and blank templates, then synthesize a formal expert workspace that can later survive deployment acceptance.

units.title: Inspect Learning Materials
units.goal: Extract the stable task obligations, data mappings, output contracts, and failure-sensitive document requirements from the workbook, expert references, and templates.
units.claim: The stable obligations and reference evidence needed for an expert workspace have been extracted.
units.check_plan: Leave concise structured scratch and learning evidence that future workspace synthesis can reuse.

units.title: Synthesize Expert Workspace
units.goal: Write a formal expert workspace that teaches a blank agent how to use the approved capability assets to go from workbook plus templates to the required Word outputs.
units.claim: The learned expert workspace is complete enough to face deployment acceptance.
units.check_plan: Update the tracked expert workspace with rules, contracts, checklists, exceptions, and tool guidance that are specific enough for deployment but abstract enough to generalize across runs.

notes: Round 2 of the real expert-experience bootstrap experiment. The platform may use multiple sessions during learning, but the final success gate is still a blank-agent single-session deployment acceptance run. This round starts from the round-1 learned expert workspace plus explicit failure evidence, without injecting task-specific execution code into the platform core.
